inline_comments.comment: This file is developer scratch notes ('Please help me to implement the tidy-tree algorithm.') and should never be committed to the repository. It contains implementation prompts, not project documentation. Please delete this file and the stray `.instructions/` entry that was added to `.gitignore`.

The r1/r2 guard condition was changed incorrectly during the refactor:

**Before:** `if (r1 !== 0 && r2 !== 0 && sameSign(r1, r2))`
**After:** `if (Math.abs(r1) < epsilon && Math.abs(r2) < epsilon && sameSign(r1, r2))`

The original condition correctly returns `undefined` (no intersection) when both endpoints of segment p lie on the **same side** of line q — i.e., both non-zero and same sign. The new condition instead fires only when both values are near-zero (both endpoints essentially ON line q), which is a completely different and much rarer scenario.

This means the normal non-intersection case is no longer caught here, so `intersectLine` will proceed to compute a spurious intersection point for line segments that do not actually cross. The r3/r4 guard above was correctly left unchanged; this r1/r2 guard must be restored to `!== 0`. This is a regression that will affect all shapes using this utility.

Setting `config.layout = 'tidy-tree'` as the default for every mindmap that lacks an explicit layout is a silent breaking change with a serious fallback problem. `tidy-tree` is **not** registered in the default layout loaders (only `dagre` and `cose-bilkent` are). When `getRegisteredLayoutAlgorithm` cannot find `tidy-tree`, it falls back to `dagre` — not `cose-bilkent`. So existing mindmap users who have not installed `@mermaid-js/layout-tidy-tree` will silently get the `dagre` layout instead of the expected `cose-bilkent`.

Options: (1) Register `tidy-tree` as a default bundled loader so it is always available, or (2) change the fallback in `mindmapRenderer.ts` to `'tidy-tree'` only when the package is present and keep `cose-bilkent` as the preprocess default, or (3) keep `cose-bilkent` as the default in preprocess and let `tidy-tree` opt-in via explicit `config.layout`.

`preferredLayout` is computed from `conf?.layoutAlgorithm` but is never assigned to `data4Layout.layoutAlgorithm`. The actual algorithm is set two lines above from `getRegisteredLayoutAlgorithm(layout, ...)`, which uses the global `layout` config only. As a result, the mindmap-specific `conf.layoutAlgorithm` setting (which was also added to `MindmapDiagramConfig` and `config.schema.yaml` in this PR) is silently ignored at runtime. Users who set `mindmap.layoutAlgorithm: 'cose-bilkent'` in their diagram frontmatter will not see their preference honored. Either remove the `preferredLayout` variable and the dead code around it, or use it: `data4Layout.layoutAlgorithm = getRegisteredLayoutAlgorithm(preferredLayout, { fallback: 'cose-bilkent' });`

This entire file (`createGraphWithElements`) is added but never imported or called anywhere in the codebase. Dead code should not be merged. Either integrate it into the rendering pipeline or delete it.

`import type { NodeChildren } from 'mermaid/dist/rendering-util/types.js'` imports from the **compiled output** (`dist/`) rather than the TypeScript source. This will break when `dist/` is stale or absent (e.g., a clean checkout before a build). Import from the source instead: `import type { NodeChildren } from 'mermaid/src/rendering-util/types.js'` — or, since this is a sibling type in the same source tree, use a relative path.

`validateLayoutData` throws `'Root node is required'` when `data.rootNode` is absent. `rootNode` is a mindmap-specific field added informally to `LayoutData` via its index signature — it is not part of the canonical interface. Registering `cose-bilkent` as a default layout (in `render.ts`) while requiring a mindmap-specific field means any non-mindmap diagram that selects `cose-bilkent` will throw immediately. Remove the `rootNode` check from `validateLayoutData`, or scope `cose-bilkent` exclusively to mindmap through the renderer rather than as a universal default.

`isGroup` is changed from `boolean` (required) to `boolean?` (optional). Per project rules, a field should not be made optional unless it genuinely can be absent. `isGroup` is used throughout the rendering pipeline in discriminated branches (`if (node.isGroup) { ... }`); making it optional means TypeScript will no longer flag callers that forgot to set it, and accidental `undefined` would be falsy-coerced to the non-group path silently. Keep it required, or add a strict `=== true` check everywhere it is tested.

There are ~15 debug statements with the personal prefix `'APA01 ...'` added in this PR, several of which perform expensive serialization (`JSON.stringify(elkGraph, null, 2)` on a potentially large graph object). Per project guidelines, excessively chatty debug logging with personal tags must be removed before merging. The same `APA01` tag also appears in `cose-bilkent/render.ts` and `tidy-tree/render.ts`. Strip all `APA01`-prefixed statements; keep only production-quality `log.debug` calls with informative messages if genuinely needed.

`cytoscape.use(coseBilkent)` is called at module scope. Since `cose-bilkent` is now a default registered loader, this line will execute every time the module is imported. If the module is ever imported more than once (e.g., via separate dynamic-import chunks or test isolation), Cytoscape will log a warning about the plugin already being registered. Move the `use()` call inside `createCytoscapeInstance` and guard it with a module-level boolean flag, or use `try/catch` to suppress the duplicate-registration warning.

`_drawNodes` is defined here but never called in the new `draw` function. The new rendering flow goes directly through `db.getData()` → `render(data4Layout, svg)`. This is dead code and should be deleted. Similarly, `_updateNodeDimensions` at line ~33 is defined but never called — also dead code. The stale comment on line ~51 (`// Draw the nodes first to get their dimensions, then update the layout data`) should also be removed as it describes the old flow, not the new one.

`let intersectionShift = 50;` is the initial declaration, but it is unconditionally overwritten to `30` a few lines later inside the `try` block before it is ever read. The initial value of `50` is dead code. Either initialize directly to `30` with `const intersectionShift = 30;` or declare it at the point of first use.

Parameters `_leftBoundingBox: any` and `_rightBoundingBox: any` (and `_data: LayoutData`) in `combineAndPositionTrees` are declared but their values are never read inside the function. Remove them from the signature to keep the function contract honest. If bounding-box information will be needed in a future iteration, add it back when actually used.

`diagramId: 'mindmap-' + Date.now()` generates the diagram ID from wall-clock time. Parallel renders or rapid consecutive calls within the same millisecond will receive the same ID, causing SVG element ID collisions. The diagram ID should come from the `id` parameter passed to the `draw` function, which the caller already provides. `getData()` does not have access to `id`, so either pass it as a parameter or let the renderer assign `data4Layout.diagramId = id` after `getData()` returns (which `mindmapRenderer.ts` already does on line ~77 — making this value immediately overwritten, which means the `Date.now()` call is both fragile and irrelevant).

This file now contains at least a dozen elements all sharing `id="diagram4"`. HTML requires IDs to be unique within a document; duplicate IDs cause `document.getElementById` and CSS selectors to return only the first match and may break Cypress test targeting. Use distinct IDs (e.g., `diagram-mindmap-tidy-1`, `diagram-mindmap-tidy-2`, …) for each test fixture block. Also, many of the new blocks use `class="mermaid2"` (not rendered by the Mermaid initializer), suggesting they are developer scratch content that should be removed before merge.

`PositionedEdge` does not declare a `points` field, yet `calculateEdgePositions` in `layout.ts` adds `points: [...]` to every returned edge object, and `render.ts` reads `positionedEdge.points` directly. The field is currently accessible only via the `[key: string]: unknown` catch-all. Declare it explicitly — `points: Array<{ x: number; y: number }>` — to make the contract clear and enable type checking at call sites.

`Edge.type` is changed from required (`type: string`) to optional (`type?: string`). This field is used throughout the rendering pipeline to distinguish edge variants. Making it optional weakens the type contract for all existing diagram renderers that set and read `edge.type`. The mindmap edges set `type: 'normal'` explicitly, so there is no need to weaken the shared interface. Keep it required.

general_comments.comment: **`mindmap.layoutAlgorithm` config option is effectively dead code.** The PR adds `layoutAlgorithm?: string` to `MindmapDiagramConfig` and to `config.schema.yaml` (with `default: 'cose-bilkent'`), strongly implying users can control the mindmap layout via this field. In practice it is never honored: `preprocess.ts` overrides `config.layout` to `'tidy-tree'` for any mindmap that lacks `config.layout`, and `mindmapRenderer.ts` reads only the global `layout` variable (not `conf.layoutAlgorithm`) when setting `data4Layout.layoutAlgorithm`. The schema default (`'cose-bilkent'`) also directly contradicts the preprocess default (`'tidy-tree'`). Either wire `conf.layoutAlgorithm` into the renderer (which `preferredLayout` was apparently meant to do but doesn't) or remove the field from the schema and config type.

**Personal debug tags left throughout multiple production files.** Strings like `'APA01 ...'`, `'APA12 ...'` appear in `mermaid-layout-elk/src/render.ts`, `cose-bilkent/render.ts`, `tidy-tree/render.ts`, and `mindmapRenderer.ts`. One instance uses `log.error` (not just `log.debug`) with this tag. Per project convention, all excessively chatty debug logging and personal developer tags must be removed before merging. Several of the `JSON.stringify(..elkGraph..)` calls are particularly expensive for any non-trivial diagram.

**`cose-bilkent` registered as a universal default layout may increase bundle size for all diagrams.** Adding `cose-bilkent` to `registerDefaultLayoutLoaders` in `render.ts` means Cytoscape and `cytoscape-cose-bilkent` are now lazily loaded for any diagram that selects the `cose-bilkent` algorithm — not just mindmaps. Previously these libraries were scoped to the mindmap module only. Because the `cose-bilkent` renderer also fails for non-mindmap diagrams (requires `rootNode`), registering it as a universal default offers no benefit while increasing the exposed surface area. Consider registering it only when rendering mindmaps, or restore the previous pattern of bundling it directly in the mindmap renderer.

**`packages/mermaid-layout-tidy-tree/README.md` contains unrendered code blocks.** The README has inline code examples for shell commands, TypeScript, and HTML that are missing their triple-backtick fences (e.g., `sh
npm install ...`, `ts
import mermaid...`, `html
<script type="module">...`). These will display as plain unformatted text on GitHub and npm. Wrap each example in a proper fenced code block with the appropriate language identifier.
